reason: The text contains multiple regular people characters who demonstrate clear agency and decision-making capacity. Most notably, Rahab (הַזּוֹנָה - the prostitute) makes an independent choice to hide the Israelite spies, conceals them from authorities, and successfully negotiates for the protection of herself and her entire family—preserving their lives through her own actions. Additionally, Joshua gives commands and makes tactical decisions about how to conduct the siege; the priests actively perform their assigned roles; the warriors (גִּבּוֹרֵי הֶחָֽיִל) execute the military strategy; and the people of Israel participate in the conquest by following instructions and shouting when commanded. Even those following orders demonstrate agency through active participation, not mere passive compliance. Rahab in particular demonstrates the most autonomous agency—she makes calculations, takes risks, and directly influences the narrative outcome.
